section_summary: This section contains internal GHQ SCAP check sheets and draft communications from June to August 1949 regarding the legal status, nationality registration, and repatriation of Korean residents in occupied Japan, culminating in General MacArthur's decision to defer action indefinitely. It also includes November 1949 correspondence involving the Japanese American Citizens League (JACL) and the Department of State protesting racial discrimination by British Commonwealth Occupation Forces (BCOF) against Japanese American (Nisei) personnel in Hiroshima. The State Department instructed the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo to pursue the matter informally with the Australian Mission.

subfiles.about: Recommendations by G-2 regarding screening procedures, nationality renunciation, and identity documentation for Koreans registering with the Korean Mission in Japan.
subfiles.from: Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Far East Command
subfiles.summary: G-2 suggests screening applicants for Korean citizenship with history forms, fingerprints, and oaths, and requiring passports or identification documents.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Government Section statement of non-objection to Diplomatic Section's staff study on Koreans in Japan despite certain reservations.
subfiles.summary: Government Section expresses reservations regarding the proposed policy for Koreans in Japan but interposes no objection in view of U.S. policy.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan (Note No. 2)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic Section request for concurrence on a staff study on Koreans in Japan, and Legal Section analysis recommending voluntary repatriation or absorption into Japanese life.
subfiles.from: Diplomatic Section and Legal Section, SCAP
subfiles.summary: Diplomatic Section requests staff concurrence on treatment of Koreans in Japan. Legal Section concurs with the proposed diplomatic reply and recommends a long-term policy based on voluntary repatriation or absorption into Japanese life.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan (Notes Nos. 1-2)
subfiles.to: Legal Section, Government Section, G-1, G-2, ESS/FIB, and Diplomatic Section, SCAP

subfiles.about: Diplomatic Section recommendations to the Chief of Staff regarding nationality, registration by the Korean Mission, and legal status of Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Diplomatic Section summarizes staff study conclusions on Korean residents in Japan, reviews staff section concurrences, and requests Chief of Staff approval for proposed communications to the Korean Mission and Washington.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status of Koreans in Japan (Note No. 1)

subfiles.about: Draft SCAP diplomatic note setting forth policy on repatriation, nationality registration, and legal status of Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: SCAP outlines its policy encouraging Korean repatriation, states unrepatriated Koreans retain Japanese nationality unless registered with the Korean Mission and released by Japanese authorities, and urges strict registration standards.
subfiles.title: Draft Note to Korean Ambassador

subfiles.about: Draft outgoing telegram reporting SCAP's position and pending reply to the Korean Ambassador concerning nationality and treatment of Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP reports to Washington and Seoul regarding its reply to the Korean Ambassador on registration and nationality of resident Koreans.
subfiles.title: Draft Radio from SCAP to Department of State and Department of the Army
subfiles.to: Department of State, Department of the Army, and American Embassy Seoul

subfiles.about: Internal GHQ SCAP debate between Government Section and Diplomatic Section regarding proposed legal distinction and registration of Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.from: Deputy Chief of Staff, SCAP; Government Section; and Diplomatic Section
subfiles.summary: Deputy Chief of Staff requests Government Section to detail its reservations regarding the proposed policy for Koreans in Japan. Government Section argues that distinguishing registered from unregistered Koreans is contrary to the Korean government's position, creates administrative and jurisdictional burdens, and should be deferred until the peace conference. Diplomatic Section rebuts these objections, maintaining that registration under SCAP guidance is legally sound, administratively feasible, and necessary to avoid indefinite deterioration of the situation.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status of Koreans in Japan (Notes Nos. 2-5)
subfiles.to: Government Section; Deputy Chief of Staff, SCAP; and Diplomatic Section

subfiles.about: Notification that the Commander in Chief and Chief of Staff decided to defer indefinitely any action on the Korean status project.
subfiles.summary: Deputy Chief of Staff informs Diplomatic Section that General MacArthur decided to defer action on Korean status indefinitely.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of protest letters sent to Australian officials concerning racial discrimination against Japanese American personnel by Australian occupation forces in Japan.
subfiles.from: Mike Masaoka (Japanese American Citizens League Anti-Discrimination Committee)
subfiles.summary: Mike Masaoka transmits protest letters sent to Australia regarding discrimination against Nisei personnel in Japan, urging State Department good offices.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mike Masaoka to Secretary of State Dean Acheson

subfiles.about: Protest against Australian occupation forces' "white only" policy excluding Japanese American scientists and technicians in Hiroshima from recreational facilities.
subfiles.from: Mike Masaoka (Japanese American Citizens League Anti-Discrimination Committee)
subfiles.summary: Mike Masaoka protests the exclusion of forty Japanese American scientists and technicians in Hiroshima from Australian-operated facilities, highlighting their wartime ATIS contributions and warning of United Nations Human Rights Commission action.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mike Masaoka to Australian Ambassador Norman J. O. Makin
subfiles.to: Norman John Oswald Makin (Ambassador of Australia)

subfiles.about: Department of State acknowledgment of Masaoka's protest regarding British Commonwealth Occupation Forces recreational policies in Japan.
subfiles.from: William P. Snow (Officer in Charge, Dominion Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: State Department acknowledges Masaoka's letter and confirms forwarding copies of the protest to United States authorities in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from William P. Snow to Mike Masaoka
subfiles.to: Mike Masaoka (Japanese American Citizens League Anti-Discrimination Committee)

subfiles.about: Recommendation to handle Masaoka's discrimination complaint informally through the Political Adviser in Tokyo and the Australian Mission.
subfiles.from: Marshall Green (Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Marshall Green agrees with Masaoka's complaint but recommends informal discussions between SCAP's Political Adviser and the Australian Mission in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Marshall Green to J. Harold Shullaw
subfiles.to: J. Harold Shullaw (Division of British Commonwealth Affairs, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Instruction transmitting Masaoka's complaint regarding Australian discrimination against Nisei researchers and suggesting informal discussions with the Australian Mission.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits Masaoka's complaint and suggests informal discussions with the Australian Mission in Tokyo regarding BCOF discrimination.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 267 to the Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
